title: Tell me your plans — the future
goal: Make plans with three ways of expressing the future, then use everything in this module in one complete conversation.
bekal: choose between the present with a time word and the *fog* form
invite, offer, and agree on plans

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Hétvégi tervek
dialogs.intro: Friday afternoon, in front of the school building. The weather is already warm; Budi's first summer in Hungary is about to begin.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.id: What are you doing this weekend?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Szombaton a Balatonra megyek a barátaimmal.
lines.id: On Saturday I'm going to Lake Balaton with my friends.
lines.literal: Saturday-on the Balaton-onto I-go the friend-PL-my-with.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.id: Great! How long are you staying there?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Vasárnap estig. Fogunk úszni és sétálni.
lines.id: Until Sunday evening. We'll swim and walk around.
lines.literal: Sunday evening-until. we-will swim and walk.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.id: What will the weather be like?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Meleg lesz, huszonnyolc fok. Nem fog esni.
lines.id: Hot, twenty-eight degrees. It won't rain.
lines.literal: hot will-be, twenty-eight degree. not it-will fall.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.id: No, only Saturday. On Sunday I'll rest.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Akkor jövő héten együtt megyünk valahova.
lines.id: Then next week let's go somewhere together.
lines.literal: then coming week-on together we-go somewhere-to.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.id: Good idea! We'll talk about it later.

notes: **Fog + infinitive is the clearest future.** *fogok, fogsz, fog, fogunk, fogtok, fognak* — only *fog* changes form, while the main verb stays in its *-ni* form. The pattern is exactly the same as the helper verbs in unit 14.

**But the present is enough when the time is clear.** *Szombaton a Balatonra megyek* and *Vasárnap pihenek* are both present, and nobody misunderstands — just like "I'm going to Balaton on Saturday" in English. The *fog* form is used when no time has been mentioned, or when you want to stress that it's a plan.

**Dolgozni fogok, or fogok dolgozni?** Both are correct. What stands **right before the verb** is the emphasized part, so *dolgozni fogok* stresses the work ("what I'll be doing is **working**"), while *fogok dolgozni* is more neutral. This is the word-order rule that has been around since unit 7, now with a new form.

**Lesz handles the future of van.** *Meleg lesz* (it will be hot), *Milyen lesz az idő?* (what will the weather be like?). Note that *lesz* doesn't need *fog* — it's already future by itself, and adding *fog* there is wrong.
**Nem fog esni** negates the future. Note that *nem* stands before *fog*, not before the main verb. The rule is the same as with all helper verbs: the negation attaches to the part that changes form.

grammars.title: The future: fog + infinitive
body: The main verb doesn't change at all; *fog* carries all the work.
after: **Fog also has a definite form**, used when the object is definite: *fogom, fogod, fogja, fogjuk, fogjátok, fogják*. Example: *Meg fogom nézni a filmet* = "I'm going to watch the film". The unit 11 rule applies here as everywhere.
**The verbal prefix stands alone in front**, following the unit 14 rule: *meg fogom nézni*, *el fogok menni*, *fel fogom hívni*.

grammars.title: Three ways to express the future
body: All three are correct. What differs is how firm the plan is.

head: Way
When it's used
Example
Meaning
rows: a plan with a clear time

after: In everyday conversation the first way is the most common — just like in English. The *fog* form sounds slightly more formal, and is required for weather forecasts, promises, and things whose timing is uncertain.
One more useful pattern: *Szeretnék…* for a wish that isn't yet a plan. *Szeretnék Szegedre menni* = "I'd like to go to Szeged" — with no promise attached.

grammars.title: Future time words
body: A mirror image of the past list in unit 18.
after: *Jövő* means "coming", and is the adjective form of *jön*. So *a jövő hét* is literally "the coming week" — and English says "the coming week" too, so it's the same logic seen from the direction of time.

head: Magyar
Say it
English
rows: I don't feel like it right now.

blocks.text: *Van kedved…?* is literally "is there your mood…?" — the possessive pattern from unit 5 used to make an offer. It's followed by an infinitive: *Van kedved moziba menni?* (Fancy going to the cinema?). This is the most natural invitation between friends, heard far more often than *Akarsz…?*, which sounds demanding.

*Menjünk!* is the first-person plural imperative — "let's". It isn't covered in this module because imperatives are A2 material, but you'll hear it every day, so recognize it now: *Menjünk!* (let's go), *Nézzük meg!* (let's have a look), *Együnk!* (let's eat).
Twenty units done. Here is what you now hold in your hands — not a list of material you've read, but a list of things you can **do**.

items: **Introduce yourself** and ask about other people: name, origin, age, job, family.
**Build sentences without a verb** for the third person — the box that stays empty in the present, where English needs "is".
**Pick the right ending** yourself through vowel harmony, without memorizing them one by one.
**Use place endings** for spaces, surfaces, and people, with their three directions each.
**Express possession** with endings, and build "have" from *van* and *nincs*.
**Shop and order**: prices, weights, units, cash or card.
**Tell the time** — hours, days, months, dates — including *fél hét*, which means 6:30 ("half toward seven").
**Conjugate present-tense verbs** in two sets, and know when to use which.
**Ask for directions** and understand the answer on the street.
**Say can, want, must, may** with the infinitive.
**Describe people and things**, compare them in two ways, and say which is the most.
**Tell about yesterday** in the past tense, including the eight irregular verbs used most.
**Make plans** with three ways of expressing the future.

blocks.text: That is a complete A1 — and more importantly, you've cleared the three hurdles that make many people stop before they get here: vowel harmony, endings that replace prepositions, and two sets of verb forms. None of the three will ever be a challenge again; all that remains is adding vocabulary and polishing forms.
The last page of this module has advice on where to go next. For now, just one sentence: *Gratulálok! Nagyon ügyes vagy!* — Congratulations! You're doing great!
